item.title: Field Notes on Reliable Agents (1): The Build Is the Only Gate
item.description:
I run a lot of long-lived agent loops — pipelines where a parent agent spawns children, each child edits a slice of a codebase, and the parent stitches the results back together. The single most expensive lesson I’ve learned is embarrassingly simple: a component reporting “green” tells you almost nothing about whether the system works.

This is the first of seven field notes on keeping such systems honest. They’re deliberately generic — none of them depend on a particular framework or model. This one is the foundation the other six build on.

item.title: Docker and Containers (8): Beyond Docker — Kubernetes, Swarm, and What Comes Next
item.description:
So far, this series has focused on single-host Docker: one machine running containers. This setup works well for development, small projects, and applications with modest traffic. However, when you need your service to survive server failures, handle traffic spikes, or deploy updates without downtime, single-host Docker falls short. Container orchestration addresses these issues, and Kubernetes has become the go-to solution.
